meta.title: AURIS — Signal analysis for AI-generated music
meta.description: Measure a track from a file, a link or your microphone: spectrogram, bandwidth, spectral periodicity and dynamic range. Your file never leaves the browser.
meta.keywords: AURIS, AI music detection, spectrogram, audio analysis, CrownCode

intro.lead: Drop in a track; AURIS measures it and shows, one reading at a time, how closely it resembles the traces generative audio models leave. It doesn't hand down a verdict — it tells you what it saw and why.
intro.localNote: Files and mic takes are measured in your browser

file.browse: or choose one from your computer
file.formats: MP3 · WAV · FLAC · M4A · OGG — up to 30 MB
file.privacy: Nothing is uploaded; it's processed in this tab.

url.label: YouTube link
url.hint: The server downloads the audio and runs the same measurements. YouTube sometimes blocks downloads; if it does, upload the file instead.
url.needsServer: Downloading audio from a link needs the AURIS server, which isn't connected right now. Upload the track as a file and the same measurement runs in your browser.

mic.hint: Play the track through a speaker and hold your device close. Recording stops by itself at 30 seconds. The room and the microphone affect the result.

scope.idle: Pick a track and its waveform and spectrogram are drawn here.

report.title: Synthetic trace score
report.scoreHint: The score is a weighted average of the seven readings below. The thresholds are hand-tuned; this is a measurement report, not a classifier.
report.lossyNote: In a lossy format (MP3, AAC…) the encoder itself cuts the high frequencies, so bandwidth was left out.
report.remoteNote: This result came from an external model:

spectralPeriodicity.label: Spectral periodicity
spectralPeriodicity.desc: Evenly spaced peaks above 4 kHz that don't move over time. Neural decoders can leave this grid when they upsample audio; musical harmonics shift with every note.

bandwidthCutoff.label: Bandwidth
bandwidthCutoff.desc: The frequency where the energy stops. Many generators cut around 16 kHz; studio recordings usually reach 20 kHz.

flatnessVariation.label: Flatness variation
flatnessVariation.desc: How much the sound moves between tonal and noisy moments. Very little movement means the texture stays the same from start to finish.

centroidVariation.label: Brightness variation
centroidVariation.desc: How far the spectral centroid wanders over the track. In a live performance it shifts clearly as instruments come and go.

loudnessRange.label: Dynamic range
loudnessRange.desc: The spread of short-term loudness (similar to LRA). A very narrow range points to heavy compression, which modern masters share.

tempoDrift.label: Tempo drift
tempoDrift.desc: The tempo difference across four sections of the track. Human playing drifts a little; grid-locked productions may not drift at all.

stereoCorrelation.label: Stereo correlation
stereoCorrelation.desc: How similar the left and right channels are. A near-mono image is common with some generators.

method.title: What is measured, and what isn't
method.lead: AURIS's trained model layer (wav2vec2) is still being developed as part of a thesis. The results on this page are signal measurements only: every number is computed from the audio you provide, with nothing random or estimated.
method.step1: The audio is decoded to 44.1 kHz stereo; for long tracks the middle 90 seconds are used.
method.step2: A short-time Fourier transform is computed with 2048-sample windows.
method.step3: Seven readings are extracted and each is placed between 0 and 1 using hand-set thresholds.
method.step4: A weighted average gives the synthetic trace score, and each reading's push on that score is shown separately.
method.limit1: Lossy compression, microphones and room acoustics distort the readings. WAV or FLAC gives the cleanest result.
method.limit2: Heavily compressed or fully electronic productions can score high even when people made them.
method.limit3: The score is not proof; don't use it alone to decide where a track came from.

meta.title: Privacy Policy - CrownCode
meta.description: What data CrownCode collects, how it is used and how it is protected.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: CrownCode respects user privacy. This policy explains our platform's data collection and usage practices.

dataCollection.title: Data Collection
dataCollection.content: CrownCode platform collects minimal data to improve user experience. This includes browser information, preferred language and theme settings. We do not collect personally identifiable information.

dataUsage.title: Data Usage
dataUsage.content: Collected data is used solely to provide platform functionality. Your data is not shared with or sold to third parties. Tools that use AI (Crown Commend, Crown Dreams) do not store user data.

dataSecurity.title: Data Security
dataSecurity.content: All data transfers are encrypted via HTTPS. Local storage (localStorage) only stores user preferences. Session data is cleared when the browser is closed.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.content: The platform uses essential cookies required for basic functionality. These cookies include language preference and theme settings. No third-party tracking cookies are used.
